children: said on Thursday it has been awarded a nearly A$800 million ($557.60 million) contract by ASX-listed DigiCo Infrastructure REIT
to expand a data centre campus in Sydney.

The contract covers a 52-megawatt expansion of the SYD1 facility, bringing the campus' total capacity to 88 MW when combined with its existing capacity and a recently completed 20-MW upgrade delivered by SHAPE.
Demand for data centre capacity has surged globally as companies ramp up investments in AI infrastructure, driving a wave of expansion projects across Australia and other major markets.
SHAPE has been appointed head contractor under a fixed-price design-and-construct contract and it said the work would begin immediately.

The project involves the adaptive reuse of an existing data centre asset with approved grid capacity, water access and development approvals already in place, allowing new capacity to be added without a greenfield development.

SHAPE, which provides refurbishment and design-and-build services to industries spanning government and defence to hotels and hospitality, said the data centre project would increase its work in hand to more than A$1.4 billion, and materially contribute to revenue in 2027 and 2028.
